description: This course explores the architecture, protocols, and security mechanisms of wireless networks, focusing on technologies such as Wi-Fi (802.11ac/ax), Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), Zigbee, and cellular networks (4G/5G). Topics include wireless communication fundamentals, network topology, mobility management, and security protocols like WPA3, TLS/DTLS, and IEEE 802.1X. Students will analyze the trade-offs between performance and security in wireless environments, design secure network configurations, and evaluate the impact of interference and signal degradation on network reliability. The course also covers advanced topics such as IoT security, wireless intrusion detection systems (WIDS), and encryption algorithms like AES and RSA. Specific methods and standards discussed include the IEEE 802.11 family, Bluetooth Core Specification, and 3GPP for 5G security frameworks.

clos.text: Define the key components of wireless network architecture, including access points, base stations, and mobility management protocols such as Mobile IP and LTE Mobility Management.
Describe the physical and MAC layer operations of Wi-Fi standards (802.11ac/ax), including OFDMA, MU-MIMO, and channel bonding techniques.
Explain the security mechanisms of WPA3, TLS/DTLS, and IEEE 802.1X, including cryptographic algorithms like AES-CCMP and RSA key exchange protocols.
Apply security best practices for wireless networks, such as implementing WPA3-Enterprise, configuring firewalls for Wi-Fi traffic, and setting up secure IoT device communication using MQTT over TLS.

Design and evaluate secure wireless network infrastructures, including the deployment of wireless intrusion detection systems (WIDS), RF jamming mitigation strategies, and the integration of 5G security protocols in enterprise environments.
Analyze the impact of interference, signal fading, and environmental factors on wireless network performance and security.
Construct secure wireless communication systems by implementing end-to-end encryption, secure authentication mechanisms, and network segmentation strategies for IoT devices.
Evaluate the trade-offs between security and performance in wireless networks, including the impact of encryption overhead on throughput and latency.
Design secure wireless network configurations for enterprise environments, including the use of VLANs, QoS policies, and secure roaming mechanisms.
Implement wireless security protocols such as EAP-TLS, PEAP, and WPA3 in lab environments using tools like Wireshark and network simulators.
Analyze and interpret wireless network traffic using packet capture tools to detect anomalies and security threats.
Construct a secure wireless network infrastructure by integrating 5G security frameworks, IoT device authentication, and RF signal analysis tools.
Evaluate the effectiveness of wireless intrusion detection systems (WIDS) in detecting and mitigating advanced threats such as rogue access points and MITM attacks.
Design and implement secure wireless communication systems for IoT applications, including secure MQTT over TLS and BLE security profiles.
Construct and evaluate secure wireless network policies and procedures for compliance with industry standards such as ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST SP 800-113.
